questions.q: What is the correct HTML to create a link that opens `https://www.example.com` in a new browser tab while preventing the new page from accessing the originating page's `window.opener` property?
questions.a: `Example` A wrong answer like omitting `rel` or using `target="new"` reveals the student doesn't know the security risk of `target="_blank"` (the new page can redirect the original page via `window.opener.location = '...'`) or confuses the `target` keyword `_blank` with a custom window name.

questions.q: A student writes `Contact` on `index.html` in the root folder. The site structure is: ``` root/ index.html pages/ contact.html ``` Why does the link fail, and how should `href` be corrected?
questions.a: The link fails because `contact.html` is inside the `pages` subfolder, not the root. The correct `href` is `pages/contact.html` (relative path from current file). A wrong answer like `../contact.html` or `/contact.html` reveals confusion about relative path resolution: `../` goes up one level (not needed here), and `/` starts from the domain root (would look for `contact.html` at the site root, not inside `pages`).

questions.q: Write the HTML for a "Back to Top" link that jumps to an `<header id="top">` on the same page. Then explain why adding `target="_blank"` to this link would be incorrect.
questions.a: `Back to Top` Adding `target="_blank"` would open the *same page* in a new tab scrolled to `#top`, instead of smoothly scrolling the current page. This reveals the student treats `target` as decorative rather than understanding it changes the browsing context — fragment identifiers (`#id`) only work within the same document context.

questions.q: Compare these two links: ```html Link A Link B ``` If both are on `https://site.org/home`, analyze where each link navigates and in which browsing context. Identify any security difference.
questions.a:
Link A: Opens `https://site.org/page?query=1#section` in a **new tab** (due to `_blank`). Without `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the new page can access `window.opener`.  
Link B: Opens `https://site.org/page?query=1#section` in the **same tab** (due to `_self`). The leading `/` makes it root-relative (resolved from domain root).  
Security difference: Link A is vulnerable to reverse-tabnabbing if `rel` is missing; Link B is not. A student who says both open in new tabs or thinks `/page` is relative to `/home` reveals misunderstanding of absolute vs root-relative URLs and `target` behavior.

questions.q: A developer argues: "Using `target="_blank"` on all external links improves UX because users don't lose the original site." Evaluate this claim considering security, accessibility, and user control. Provide a balanced recommendation.
questions.a:
The claim is partially valid but dangerous without mitigation.  
Security: `target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"` allows the external site to redirect the original page (tabnabbing).  
Accessibility: Screen readers may not announce new tabs; users with cognitive disabilities can be disoriented.  
User control: Modern browsers let users choose (right-click → "Open in new tab"); forcing it removes agency.  
Recommendation: Use `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` **only** for links where context loss is high risk (e.g., interrupting a form), and add an icon/aria-label indicating "opens in new tab". A student who agrees unconditionally misses security/accessibility; one who rejects entirely misses legitimate UX cases.

questions.q:
Design a navigation menu for a portfolio site with these requirements:  
- "Home" links to `index.html` (root)  
- "Projects" links to `projects/index.html` (subfolder)  
- "Contact" opens `mailto:me@example.com`  
- "Resume" opens `assets/resume.pdf` in a new tab  
- "Top" jumps to `<main id="top">`  
Write the complete `<nav>` HTML with semantic structure. Justify each `href` and `target` choice.
questions.a:
```html
  • Home
  • Projects
  • Contact
  • Resume
  • Top
``` Justification: - `index.html` and `projects/index.html` are relative paths from current file (assumed in root). - `mailto:` launches default email client. - PDF in new tab (`_blank`) lets user keep portfolio open; `rel` prevents tabnabbing. - `#top` is a fragment identifier for in-page scroll. A poor answer uses absolute URLs for internal links, omits `rel` on PDF, or uses `target="_self"` on the fragment link (harmless but redundant).
